# Account Registration Form Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users, keyboard-only users, low vision users, cognitive accessibility users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), keyboard-only navigation **Feature:** Multi-section account registration form with conditional fields, inline help text, expandable guidance, and field-level validation **Risk Level:** High (financial services context, complex progressive disclosure, regulated data collection) **Component/Page Type:** Complex Form with Progressive Disclosure & Dynamic State Management --- ## Scope & Context This plan covers the accessibility design for a new financial services account registration form. The form collects personal and business information, uses conditional field revelation based on account type selection, provides inline help text, expandable guidance, and field-level validation errors. **Key Ambiguity Resolution:** The design spec does not specify whether help text should be announced immediately on focus or only on demand. **Decision:** All static help text will be associated via `aria-describedby` and announced automatically on field focus. Financial/regulatory forms require guaranteed access to instructional content; the verbosity trade-off is acceptable because missing password rules or Tax ID definitions could cause submission failures or compliance issues. This aligns with WCAG 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions) and WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships). **Compliance Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA **Assistive Tech Requirements:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, keyboard-only navigation, screen magnifier support **Constraints:** React + Formik state management; no existing a11y implementation; CSS `display: none`/`block` for conditional fields --- ## Semantic Structure Plan The form uses native HTML `
` semantics with `
` and `` to group related inputs. Landmarks include a skip link, main content region, and form section heading hierarchy. ### Structure Diagram ```html Skip to registration form

Create Account

Account Information

Account Type

Personal Details

Business Details

Company Information
``` --- ## Interaction Pattern Design Every interactive element maps to a WAI-ARIA APG pattern. Keyboard models are defined for each widget. ### Interactive Elements Table | Widget | APG Pattern | Keyboard Model | ARIA Attributes | WCAG Citation | |--------|-------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------| | Account Type Radio Group | APG Radio Button Group | Tab to group, Arrow keys navigate options, Enter/Space selects | `role="radiogroup"`, `aria-labelledby` on group, `aria-checked` on radios | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Standard Inputs (Name, Email, Password) | APG Text Input | Tab to input, Enter submits form if focused | `type`, `name`, `required`, `aria-invalid` (on error), `aria-describedby` (error + help) | 1.3.1 Info & Relationships, 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions | | Expandable Help Button (`?`) | APG Disclosure (Show/Hide) | Tab to button, Enter/Space toggles panel, Escape closes if open | `aria-expanded="false"`, `aria-controls="tax-id-help"`, `aria-label="What is a Tax ID?"` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 2.1.1 Keyboard | | Submit Button | APG Button | Tab to button, Enter/Space activates | `type="submit"` (implicit role) | 2.1.1 Keyboard | | "Same as primary phone" Checkbox | APG Checkbox | Tab to checkbox, Space toggles | `type="checkbox"`, `aria-checked` (optional, native handles it), `aria-disabled` on dependent field | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | --- ## Focus Management Plan 1. **Tab Order:** Logical top-to-bottom reading order. Skip link jumps to `
`. 2. **Conditional Field Focus Movement:** When "Business Account" is selected, focus moves programmatically to the first revealed field (`#company-name`). This follows APG Progressive Disclosure pattern and WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order. A `aria-live="polite"` region announces "Business details section revealed" for users who prefer not to have focus moved. 3. **Expandable Help:** Focus remains on the `?` button when help expands. The panel is discovered via `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`. No focus movement occurs. 4. **Form Submission/Validation:** On invalid submit, focus moves to the first field with an error. This follows WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification. 5. **Focus Indicators:** Default browser outlines are sufficient (3:1 contrast). Custom focus rings use `outline` + `box-shadow` for visibility across all themes. `:focus-visible` used to avoid rings on mouse clicks. --- ## State Communication Design ### Ambiguity Resolution: Help Text Announcement Strategy **Decision:** Use `aria-describedby` with multiple IDs for all static help text. **Justification:** Financial services forms contain actionable regulatory instructions. Users cannot be expected to request help on demand; critical guidance must be guaranteed. `aria-describedby` ensures help is announced automatically after the label and input type, per WCAG 3.3.2. The verbosity trade-off is acceptable because missing password rules or Tax ID definitions directly impacts form completion success and compliance. ### Announcement Order Rule Screen readers announce `aria-describedby` values in DOM order. To ensure errors are heard before guidance: ```html ``` **Order:** Error ID first, help text ID second. NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver will announce: "Email address, edit, invalid value. Email is already in use. Must be a valid email format." ### State Communication Table | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------------| | Help text visible | Blue/gray text below input | Linked via `aria-describedby` | `aria-describedby="field-help"` | 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions, 1.3.1 Info & Relationships | | Validation error (inline) | Red border + exclamation icon + red text | `aria-invalid="true"` on input, `role="alert"`/`aria-live="assertive"` on error container | `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` | 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Conditional field hidden | `display: none` or React conditional render | Removed from accessibility tree entirely | None needed (DOM removal handles it) | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Conditional field revealed | `display: block` or React mount | `aria-live="polite"` region announces reveal, focus moves to first field | `role="region"`, `aria-live="polite"` | 4.1.3 Status Messages, 2.4.3 Focus Order | | Expandable help closed | `?` button visible, panel hidden | `aria-expanded="false"` on button | `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Expandable help open | Panel visible below field | `aria-expanded="true"` on button, content revealed via DOM/conditional render | `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Auto-filled Phone disabled | Grayed out input, cursor disabled | HTML `disabled` attribute (not `aria-disabled`) | `disabled` | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 2.1.1 Keyboard | --- ## Visual Accessibility Plan 1. **Color Contrast:** All text meets 4.5:1 (normal) or 3:1 (large). Focus indicators meet 3:1 against adjacent colors. 2. **Non-Color Indicators:** Errors use red border + exclamation icon + explicit text ("Email is already in use"). Help text uses blue/gray color + info icon + explicit text. Color is never the sole indicator per WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color. 3. **Touch Targets:** All interactive elements (radio buttons, checkboxes, buttons, `?` toggle) meet 44x44 CSS pixels minimum per WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size. 4. **Responsive Text:** Uses `rem` units. Base font 16px = 1rem. Tested at 200% zoom with no horizontal scroll (WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.10). 5. **Animation/Motion:** No animations used for state changes.
